quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is usually the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Speed up to increase distance between you and the tailgater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up makes things more dangerous because they may continue tailgating at a higher speed.

questions.question: What must an effective eye or face shield do?

options.text: Prevent all air from passing through.
Not allow eyeglasses to fit underneath.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fasten securely.
questions.explanation: An effective eye or face shield must be free of scratches, resist penetration, allow clear views to both sides, fasten securely, allow air to pass through to prevent fogging, and allow room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: Which is NOT a purpose of good lane positioning?

options.text: Help you avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
Make it easier for others to see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
questions.explanation: Good lane position should help you see and be seen, keep you out of other drivers' blind spots, help you avoid surface hazards, protect your lane from other drivers, show your intentions to others, help you avoid wind blasts from other vehicles, and give you an escape route if hazards appear.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Which is NOT required for an effective eye or face shield?
questions.correctAnswerText: Airtight.
questions.explanation: An effective eye or face shield must be free of scratches, resist penetration, give clear views to both sides, fasten securely, allow air to pass through, and permit eyeglasses or sunglasses to be worn underneath.

questions.question: How much alcohol can the body eliminate per hour?
questions.correctAnswerText: About one drink
questions.explanation: On average, a person's body can eliminate the alcohol from about one drink per hour.

questions.question: Which provides a rider with the best protection?
questions.correctAnswerText: A face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield or eyeglasses cannot replace goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?

options.text: Move to the edge of the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed, avoid sudden moves, stay away from the road edge, and ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.question: Which does NOT help reduce serious injury in a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Have a windshield.
questions.explanation: To reduce injury risk when riding a motorcycle, wear an approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake pedal usually located on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right footrest
questions.explanation: The rear brake of a motorcycle is usually controlled by a pedal near the right footrest.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: You can go over the speed limit until you finish passing.
You can ignore "No passing zone" signs if you started passing in a legal zone.
You can pass on the shoulder.
You must pass within the speed limit and only in legal passing zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must pass within the speed limit and only in legal passing zones.
questions.explanation: Always pass within the speed limit. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, they should:

options.text: Lean the same way you lean.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean the same way you lean.
questions.explanation: Your passenger should lean with you through turns and curves. They should sit as far forward as comfort allows, without blocking your control. They should hold onto the handholds, your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Each lane of traffic gives a motorcycle ____ riding path(s).
questions.correctAnswerText: Three
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane has three riding positions for a motorcycle: left, center, and right. Be ready to change your position to match road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: A danger of braking too hard is:

options.text: Losing grip on one or both wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing grip on one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: Braking too hard can make you lose traction on one or both wheels and crash.

questions.question: You should choose a lane position that:

options.text: Reduces your safety space and helps others see you.
Increases your safety space and helps others see you.
Increases your chance of hitting hazards and lets others pass.
Reduces hazards but requires you to follow other vehicles closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases your safety space and helps others see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that gives you more safety space around your motorcycle. This helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It also tells other drivers not to share your lane and gives you an escape route if needed. Always maximize your safety space.

questions.question: One sign that your rear tire has gone flat while riding is:

options.text: A hissing sound from the rear.
The back end jerks side to side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back end jerks side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire fails, the back of your motorcycle will jerk from side to side. You will rarely hear a tire fail.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake control usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right foot.
questions.explanation: The rear brake is usually operated with your right foot.

questions.question: Why should a load be placed low on a motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the center of gravity.
A high load may block the turn signals.
A high load can block your view.
Others cannot see a low load.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: Placing a load too high raises your motorcycle's center of gravity and makes it harder to balance.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Stay calm, keep a steady speed, and ride straight.
Grip the handlebars tightly and speed up to get past it.
Ride on the shoulder to avoid the grooves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm, keep a steady speed, and ride straight.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is usually not dangerous. Just relax and ride straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging to fight the weaving is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: To lower your chance of a crash, you should:

options.text: Skip your turn signals when changing lanes.
Watch only five feet ahead while riding.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure others can see you. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position correctly. Keep a safety space around your motorcycle. Watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you. Always be ready to avoid a hazard.

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and hay fever medications usually affect your body?

options.text: They make you unable to concentrate.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: Most medications for headaches, colds, hay fever, and allergies can make you drowsy. This affects your ability to ride safely. Always know how a medication affects you before you ride.

questions.question: A person with a minimum blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ is considered legally intoxicated.
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: A person age 21 or older with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to operate any vehicle while intoxicated.

questions.question: A motorcyclist's cushion of space:

options.text: Should change based on riding conditions.
Is not necessary in most situations.
Should be avoided to keep traffic moving safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should change based on riding conditions.
questions.explanation: You need more space if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Increase your following distance if the road is slippery, visibility is poor, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: If you are not traveling slowly enough when shifting into a lower gear, what could happen?

options.text: Your motorcycle may lurch and the rear tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may lurch and the front tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may lurch and a warning light will go on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may lurch and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear while going too fast, your motorcycle may lurch and the rear tire may skid. This causes you to lose control. Always slow down enough before downshifting.

questions.question: A thorough check of your motorcycle:

options.text: Is useless unless done by a mechanic.
Should not be done before a ride.
Should be done only after a ride.
Can help you find mechanical problems or equipment failures.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help you find mechanical problems or equipment failures.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride. This helps you find mechanical problems or equipment failures that could put you in danger.
